newsitem.title: USA: GTE files suit over Penn. phone ruling.
newsitem.headline: GTE files suit over Penn. phone ruling.

text.p: GTE Corp said Thursday it filed suit in a U.S. court to overturn a decision by Pennsylvania regulators governing the terms by which AT&T Corp can hook up to GTE's local phone network in the state.
"We don't think the commission did its job," GTE General Counsel William Barr told reporters in a teleconference, referring to the decision by the Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission.

The suit appears to be the first by a local phone company seeking to overturn a decision by state regulators governing the terms and conditions under which new entrants to the local phone market can hook up to the local network.
The Pennsylvania commission's interim order required GTE to lease its local network at a 22.8-percent discount, according to GTE.
It also ordered GTE to offer individual elements of its network -- such as call-switching devices and directory assistance -- at an effective 64-percent discount, GTE said.
"The Pennsylvania Commission didn't follow the (new telecommunications) act," Barr said in a statement. The suit was filed by a GTE unit, GTE North Inc.

"Instead of taking into account the evidence of GTE North's actual costs," Barr added, the Pennsylvania commission improperly relied on the Federal Communications Commission's "unlawful proxy prices, which have been stayed by the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit and which a number of proceedings throughout the country have shown to be wildly arbitrary."
Barr then accused Pennsylvania regulators of setting prices that were "grossly unfair" and "far below" those called for by the new communications law.
"The Pennsylvania commission's order is nothing more than corporate welfare for AT&T," Barr added.
Barr hinted that GTE also was prepared to file suit against other state regulators whose arbitration decisions were considered unfair.
